# Documentation useAnimations is a free, MIT-licensed library of 300 animated icons for React. Every icon comes with a built-in interaction: it loops, plays on click or plays on hover. Use them with the `react-useanimations` package or add them with the shadcn CLI.
## Quick start ```bash npm install react-useanimations ``` ```jsx import UseAnimations from 'react-useanimations'; import github from 'react-useanimations/lib/github'; export default function Header() { return ; } ``` The icon follows the text color and plays its own interaction: `github` loops while you hover it. The package has no dependencies; a built-in player (8 kB gzipped) draws the icons as SVG, and each icon is a separate module, so your bundle only includes the icons you import. ## Interactions Every icon comes with the interaction it was designed for. Override it with the `interaction` prop. | Interaction | What it does | Example icons | | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ | | `loop` | Plays continuously. | `loading`, `activity`, `alertCircle` | | `click-toggle` | Switches between two states on click (forward, then backward). | `menu`, `checkBox`, `playPause` | | `click-replay` | Replays from the start on every click. | `download`, `refresh`, `send` | | `hover` | Plays forward on mouse enter and backward on mouse leave. | `archive`, `settings`, `trash` | | `hover-loop` | Loops while hovered and finishes the current cycle on mouse leave. | `github`, `twitter`, `dribbble` | | `hover-replay` | Plays once from the start on mouse enter. | `arrowRight`, `bluetooth`, `zap` | When the user prefers reduced motion, icons stay still: loops show their first frame, hover and replay animations don't play, and toggles switch to their new state immediately.
## Props ```jsx ``` | Prop | Default | Description | | ------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `animation` | — | Icon imported from `react-useanimations/lib/`, or `{ animationData, interaction }` for your own animation. | | `size` | `24` | Width and height; numbers are pixels, strings are any CSS length such as `'1.5em'`. | | `strokeColor` | `'currentColor'` | Color of the strokes. By default the icon follows the text color. | | `fillColor` | `strokeColor` | Color of filled parts, e.g. a liked heart. | | `interaction` | per icon | `'loop'`, `'click-toggle'`, `'click-replay'`, `'hover'`, `'hover-loop'` or `'hover-replay'`. | | `active` | — | For `click-toggle` icons: `true` shows the end state. Controlled: set it in `onClick`, clicks don't toggle it. | | `autoplay` | per icon | `true` for `loop` icons, unless reduced motion is preferred. | | `loop` | per icon | `true` for `loop` and `hover-loop` icons. | | `speed` | `1` | Playback speed. | | `render` | — | Render prop for a custom wrapper, see [Wrap the icon in a real button](#wrap-the-icon-in-a-real-button). | Any other prop (`className`, `aria-label`, `onClick`, …) goes to the wrapper ``. Your event handlers run before the animation's; call `event.preventDefault()` to skip the animation. ## Importing icons Import each icon from `react-useanimations/lib/`, or several at once from `react-useanimations/icons`: ```jsx import { github, heart, menu } from 'react-useanimations/icons'; ``` Production builds include only the icons you use either way. Dev servers and test runners don't tree-shake, so there `react-useanimations/icons` loads every icon; prefer `lib/` if that matters. `delete` and `package` are reserved words: import them as `deleteIcon` and `packageIcon`. ## Controlled toggle ```jsx import { useState } from 'react'; import UseAnimations from 'react-useanimations'; import menu from 'react-useanimations/lib/menu'; export function MenuButton() { const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); return ( setOpen(!open)} /> ); } ``` ## Wrap the icon in a real button For clickable icons, put a focusable element around the icon with the `render` prop: `eventProps` go on your element and `animationProps` on a `` inside it. Hover animations then also play when the button gets keyboard focus. ```jsx import heart from 'react-useanimations/lib/heart'; ( )} />; ```
## Size & color Icons are line icons drawn on a 24 or 32 px artboard and stay sharp at any size: set `size` to a number of pixels or any CSS length. The strokes follow `currentColor`, so icons pick up the text color, hover states and dark mode on their own. Change them with `strokeColor` and `fillColor`, with CSS `color`, or style the paths: the built-in rule has zero specificity, so your CSS always wins. Some icons cut a gap into themselves (the slash in `visibility`, `microphone`, `video`, `volume` and `notification`, the check in `download`, the ring around `notification3`'s badge). The gap takes the page background: white on light pages and dark on pages with `color-scheme: dark`. On other backgrounds, set it with the `--ua-knockout` CSS variable, e.g. `body { --ua-knockout: #0f172a; }`. ```jsx // Tailwind: color and stroke width ``` ## Next.js and server rendering The component is marked `'use client'` and draws the animation only in the browser, so you can render it from server components and SSR frameworks (Next.js, Remix, Astro) without `dynamic(…, { ssr: false })`. Icon modules are plain data, so server components can import them and pass them as props.
## shadcn/ui Every icon is also in a [shadcn registry](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/registry). The CLI adds a ready-made component and installs `react-useanimations`: ```bash npx shadcn@latest add https://useanimations.com/r/checkmark.json ``` ```tsx import { AnimatedCheckmark } from '@/components/animations/checkmark'; ; ``` The component is named `Animated` + the icon id in PascalCase (`check-box` → `AnimatedCheckBox`), lands in `components/animations/.tsx` and takes the same props as `UseAnimations`. The registry index is [/r/registry.json](/r/registry.json). For the short form `npx shadcn@latest add @useanimations/checkmark`, add the registry to `components.json`: ```json { "registries": { "@useanimations": "https://useanimations.com/r/{name}.json" } } ``` ## Your own animation ```jsx import animationData from './my-animation.json'; ; ``` Your animation must be a Lottie JSON file, the format the icons use. The player supports what the icons need: shape layers, precompositions, null layers and parenting, paths, rectangles, ellipses, strokes, fills, trim paths, masks, keyframes with easing, holds and motion paths, and the `loopOut()` and `wiggle()` expressions. Anything else, such as gradients, text or image layers, effects and mattes, is not drawn; the console warns about unsupported layers, shapes and expressions.
## Files & icons.json Every icon can also be downloaded, from its page or from stable, CORS-enabled URLs: | File | URL | | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | | Animation (Lottie JSON) | `https://useanimations.com/icons/.json` | | Static SVG of each state | `https://useanimations.com/icons//.svg` | | ZIP with the JSON and SVGs | `https://useanimations.com/icons/.zip` | | Icon page | `https://useanimations.com/icons/` | | Catalog of every icon | `https://useanimations.com/icons.json` | [icons.json](/icons.json) lists every icon with its id, title, category, search keywords, interaction, file URLs, size and duration, its `react-useanimations` import and the shadcn command. The npm package ships the same data: `react-useanimations/catalog.json` (metadata), `react-useanimations/icons` (the animations) and `react-useanimations/svg.json` (the static SVGs).
## Use without React The icons are standard Lottie JSON, so any Lottie player can play them from `https://useanimations.com/icons/.json` or from a copy in your project. Outside React you wire up the interaction yourself. [Lottie icons](/lottie-icons) has more players and examples. Some icons use After Effects expressions (`loopOut()`, `wiggle()`); `requiresFullPlayer` marks them in [icons.json](/icons.json). On the web they need lottie-web's full build, not `lottie_light`, and native players don't evaluate expressions.
### HTML and JavaScript ```html
``` With the SVG renderer, the icon can follow the text color like the React component: ```css #icon path[stroke^='rgb']:not([stroke='rgb(255,255,255)']) { stroke: currentColor; } #icon path[fill='rgb(0,0,0)'] { fill: currentColor; } ```
### Vue ```vue ``` ### React Native ```jsx import LottieView from 'lottie-react-native'; ; ```
### iOS With [lottie-ios](https://github.com/airbnb/lottie-ios) and the JSON in your app bundle: ```swift import Lottie import SwiftUI LottieView(animation: .named("loading")) .looping() .frame(width: 48, height: 48) ```
### Android With [lottie-android](https://github.com/airbnb/lottie-android) in Jetpack Compose and the JSON in `res/raw`: ```kotlin val composition by rememberLottieComposition(LottieCompositionSpec.RawRes(R.raw.loading)) LottieAnimation(composition, iterations = LottieConstants.IterateForever, modifier = Modifier.size(48.dp)) ``` ### Flutter With the [lottie](https://pub.dev/packages/lottie) package: ```dart Lottie.asset('assets/loading.json', width: 48, height: 48) ```
## Performance & accessibility - **Small:** the player is 8 kB gzipped with no dependencies, and an icon is 1 to 15 kB (2 kB median). - **Lazy:** animations are drawn only in the browser, after the page renders; autoplaying loops pause while they are scrolled out of view, and everything is cleaned up on unmount. - **Decorative by default:** icons are hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`) unless you pass `aria-label`, which announces them as an image. For icon-only controls, use a real ` )} ``` Icons are now hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`) unless you pass `aria-label`; add one to icons that carry meaning on their own. ### 6. Check the icons whose interaction changed Interactions now match useanimations.com. If an icon should behave as in v2, pass its old interaction: | Icons | v2 | v3 | | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | -------------- | | `arrowDownCircle`, `arrowLeftCircle`, `arrowRightCircle`, `arrowUpCircle` | `click-toggle` | `click-replay` | | `calendar`, `folder`, `home`, `instagram`, `userMinus`, `userPlus`, `userX`, `youtube`, `youtube2` | `hover-replay`\* | `hover` | | `behance`, `codepen`, `facebook`, `github`, `linkedin`, `pocket`, `twitter` | `hover-replay`\* | `hover-loop` | | `copy`, `edit`, `mail` | `click-replay` | `hover` | | `dribbble` | `hover` | `hover-loop` | | `zoomIn`, `zoomOut` | `loop` | `hover` | \* v2 played these once on mouse enter and jumped back to the start on mouse leave; `hover-replay` is the closest. ```jsx ``` ### 7. Update imports Import icons only as `react-useanimations/lib/` or from `react-useanimations/icons`. Internal file paths of v2 such as `react-useanimations/lib/github/index` or `react-useanimations/lib/github/github.json` no longer resolve; the Lottie JSON is the icon's `animationData`: ```diff - import githubJson from 'react-useanimations/lib/github/github.json'; + import github from 'react-useanimations/lib/github'; + const githubJson = github.animationData; ``` The `react-useanimations/utils` paths were removed. Import the types from the package: ```diff - import type { Animation, AnimationKey } from 'react-useanimations/utils'; + import type { Animation, AnimationKey, Interaction, UseAnimationsProps } from 'react-useanimations'; ``` `Animation` is now `{ animationData, interaction }`; v2's `animationKey` field is gone, so objects you built yourself use `interaction` instead. ### What else is new 221 more icons (300 in total), several icons at once from `react-useanimations/icons`, reduced-motion support, hover on keyboard focus, no stuck hover animations on touch screens, server rendering without workarounds, and a [shadcn registry](#shadcnui). ## License The icons and the code are released under the [MIT license](https://opensource.org/license/mit/): use, modify and redistribute them in personal and commercial work. Attribution is not required but appreciated: ```html Animated icons by useAnimations ``` Full terms: [Licencing & Terms](/licencing-and-terms). ## FAQ
Is useAnimations free for commercial projects? Yes. The icons and the package are MIT-licensed, with no attribution required.
How do I change the color of an icon? Icons follow the text color. Change it with `strokeColor` and `fillColor`, CSS `color`, or by styling the paths. See [Size & color](#size--color).
Does it work without React? The package is for React. Every icon is also a Lottie JSON file that lottie-web, lottie-ios, lottie-android, Flutter and React Native can play, and a static SVG. See [Use without React](#use-without-react) and [Lottie icons](/lottie-icons).
Can AI coding agents use useAnimations? Yes. Point them at [icons.json](/icons.json) and [/documentation.md](/documentation.md); the package itself ships `catalog.json` and documented types for every icon.
